the development, implementation and application of automated crystallography methods at SSRL.
the development and application of new experimental methods for macromolecular X-ray crystallography.
the design and development of novel methods for the automated collection and processing of macromolecular crystal data.

the new paradigm for macromolecule crystallography at SSRL has been a resounding success.
the SSRL has a very good X-ray source and the beamline staff are very knowledgeable.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have successfully developed and implemented a system that has increased the efficiency of our macromolecular crystal-lography experiments by a factor of 10, and that we now have a robust system for the future.
we have successfully automated the entire process of macromolecular crystal screening and remote X-ray diffraction data collection.
we are now routinely collecting data from crystals of biological macromolecules that were never before thought to be amenable to X-ray diffraction studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of a flexible control software, a robust mechanized system for data collection, and an intuitive user interface has enabled the automation of crystal screening and data collection at SSRL, and has made it possible for a large fraction of the users to perform their experiments remotely.
the combination of mechanization, automation, and a flexible control and user interface allows for the rapid development of a robust system that can be used by the majority of the user community.
it is possible to perform high-quality macromolecular crystal data collection in an automated fashion, with the majority of the data collection being performed from remote locations.
